intro: Convert kilonewtons (kN) to pounds-force (lbf) accurately for climbing carabiner ratings (22–25 kN), structural beam shear loads, and rigging tension specs. Under standard gravity (9.80665 m/s²), 1 kilonewton (1,000 N) equals 224.80894 pounds-force—multiply kN by 224.80894, or tap Swap to switch from lbf to kN. Scan common force ratings from 1 kN to 500 kN below.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Kilonewtons (kN) vs. Kips (kip = 1,000 lbf) & Pounds-Mass (lbm)
items: Do not confuse kilonewtons (kN) with kips (kilopounds-force): 1 kN equals 224.81 lbf, whereas 1 kip equals 1,000 lbf (4.44822 kN)—over four times larger.
Kilonewtons and pounds-force measure mechanical force, not mass (lbm); under standard Earth gravity (9.80665 m/s²), 1 kN equals the weight of roughly 101.97 kg (224.81 lb).

faqs.question: What are kilonewtons?
faqs.answer: A kilonewton (kN) is an SI metric unit of force equal to 1,000 newtons. One kilonewton equals 224.80894 pounds-force (lbf), or roughly the gravitational force exerted by a 101.97 kg (224.8 lb) mass on Earth. Climbing gear, rigging, and structural beams are rated in kN.

faqs.question: How many lbs (lbf) are in a kilonewton?
faqs.answer: There are 224.80894 pounds-force (lbf) in 1 kilonewton (kN). Conversely, 1 pound-force equals 0.00444822 kilonewtons.

faqs.question: What is 25 kN in pounds-force?
faqs.answer: 25 kilonewtons (a standard climbing carabiner major-axis strength rating) equals 5,620.22358 pounds-force (about 5,620 lbf).

faqs.question: Is a kilonewton (kN) the same as a kip?
faqs.answer: No—a kip (kilopound-force) equals 1,000 pounds-force (4.44822 kN), whereas 1 kilonewton equals 224.80894 pounds-force.
